rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for technical terminology used in a subject or profession.

example.english: The report contains too much jargon, so laypeople are completely confused.
example.traditional: 份報告入面有太多專業術語，外行人睇到一頭霧水。
example.jyutping: fan2 bou3 gou3 jap6 min6 jau5 taai3 do1 zyun1 jip6 seot6 jyu5 ngoi6 hang4 jan4 tai2 dou3 jat1 tau4 mou6 seoi2

rows.note: Use this when the language marks membership in a particular group, rather than merely belonging to a technical field.

example.english: This is our industry's jargon, so customers may not understand it.
example.traditional: 呢啲係我哋行內嘅行話，客人未必聽得明。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 hai6 ngo5 dei6 hong6 noi6 ge3 hong4 waa2 haak3 jan4 mei6 bit1 ting1 dak1 ming4

rows.note: Use this only when the speech is genuinely nonsensical or unintelligible, not merely specialized.

example.english: After getting drunk, he spouted jargon that no one could understand.
example.traditional: 佢醉酒後講埋晒啲胡言亂語，冇人聽得明。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zeoi3 zau2 hau6 gong2 maai4 saai3 di1 wu4 jin4 lyun6 jyu5 mou5 jan4 teng1 dak1 ming4
